title: Arkansas hunting licenses, WMA permits, and fees
intro: A hunting license is required to hunt in Arkansas. Many WMAs require additional deer/turkey permits drawn through AGFC. Public-land elk is a separate resident-only draw. Confirm current fees before you buy.

whereToBuy.title: Online
whereToBuy.body: Buy licenses and apply for WMA permits at https://www.agfc.com/licenses/.

whereToBuy.title: License agent
whereToBuy.body: AGFC license agents sell hunting licenses statewide.

whereToBuy.title: WMA permit draw
whereToBuy.body: WMA deer/turkey permit applications typically open June 1–July 1. Leftovers may be offered later.

whereToBuy.title: Public-land elk draw
whereToBuy.body: Apply under Special Hunt Applications for Buffalo River / Gene Rush / Bearcat Hollow public elk (residents only). Details: https://www.agfc.com/hunting/more-game/elk/

whereToBuy.title: Over the counter
whereToBuy.body: Private-land deer seasons do not need a WMA permit; public land often does. Private-land elk permits sell OTC in the Core Elk Zone.

whereToBuy.title: Corps of Engineers lakes
whereToBuy.body: Corps project lands may allow public hunting under AGFC seasons with lake-specific restrictions.

deadlines.name: Public-land elk applications open
deadlines.detail: Online Special Hunt Applications for public-land elk (residents only).

deadlines.name: Public-land elk application deadline
deadlines.detail: Deadline 11:59 p.m.; draws include Buffalo River Elk Festival on-site permits.

residencyRules: Public-land elk permits (Buffalo National River, Gene Rush WMA, Bearcat Hollow WMA, Richland Valley Sonny Varnell) are Arkansas residents only — applicants need a Resident Sportsman’s Hunting License or Lifetime Sportsman’s Permit.

Nonresidents may hunt elk only on private land in the Core Elk Management Zone (Boone, Carroll, Madison, Newton, and Searcy counties) with a Nonresident Annual Hunting License plus a $300 Nonresident Elk Permit (NRE).
Nonresidents hunting bear, turkey, alligator, or elk need the matching nonresident add-on permit in addition to the Nonresident Annual All Game Hunting License.
Most WMA deer/turkey seasons and draws are open to properly licensed nonresidents; always confirm the specific WMA permit rules.
